gloss: handover briefing; passing on information; report

definitions.explanation: communicating important information from one person or shift to another, especially in workplaces

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{送|おく}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れないで→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't forget to do the handover briefing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜勤|やきん}→夜勤：09549_yakin⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{日勤|にっきん}→日勤：18684_nikkin⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There's a handover briefing from the night shift to the day shift.

examples.japanese: ⟦{患者|かんじゃ}→患者：00170_kanja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{伝|つた}えた→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: I communicated the patient's condition during the handover.

{申|もう}し{送|おく}る (to pass on information, to hand over)

WORKPLACE USAGE:
{申|もう}し{送|おく}り is especially common in hospitals, care facilities, and factories with shift work. It ensures continuity of care or operations. ⟦{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ→引き継ぎ：08365_hikitsugi⟧} tends to be used for longer-term handovers (job changes), while {申|もう}し{送|おく}り is often for daily or shift-based information transfer.
